newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--GDP, Chicago PMI and U of Mich.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--GDP, Chicago PMI and U of Mich.

text.p: U.S. credit markets are expected to shrug off a handful of economic data slated for release on Friday, analysts said.

The Commerce Department is scheduled to release its second estimate of first-quarter Gross Domestic Product at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists in a Reuters poll forecast a 6.0-percent annual growth rate for the period, up from its 5.6 -percent advance first quarter reading.
The Treasury market is looking for a higher revision to first-quarter GDP, said Matthew Alexy, chief markets strategist at Credit Suisse First Boston.
"It's a question of whether final sales get revised significantly or not," Alexy said, adding that "we're saying that they're not."
An upward revision -- of a few tenths -- to GDP may cause bond prices to drop initially, but any move would not be significant, analysts said.
"When GDP is revised up, initially there will be a small negative reaction but not a big one," said Sung Won Sohn, chief economist at Norwest Corp.
Sohn said the market is really focused on France's second round of parliamentary elections on Sunday and next week's employment report set for release on June 6.
"Because the market is focused on next week, that limits the range in which bond prices will fluctuate," added Sohn.

While market experts projected an upward revision to the headline GDP number, they forecast no change in the chain-weighted price index and implicit deflator, which hit 2.7 percent and 2.3 percent last month, respectively.
Indices of regional manufacturing activity, consumer sentiment and new home sales also await market attention Friday morning.

The Chicago purchasing managers survey, scheduled for release at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, is widely regarded as the best indicator of the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) nationwide index -- to be published on Monday.
Economists projected Chicago PMI would read 56.8 in May, slightly below its April reading of 57.2.
The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index is expected to register 104.0 for its May final reading, up from the previous month's 101.4 reading.
The Commerce Department will issue April single-family home sales at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Economists forecast new home sales at 800,000 units, lower than 813,000 units in March.

"It's perfectly likely that we get some disruptions in housing," said Dan Seto, senior economist at The Nikko Securities Co International Inc, referring to weather problems, such as heavy flooding in the Midwest.
"But these are likely to be temporary factors," Seto added.
Two Federal Reserve Bank officials are scheduled to speak on Friday, but are not expected to arouse market excitement.

New York Federal Reserve President William McDonough discusses "the case for price stability" to the international congress of the Association Cambiste Internacional and the Financial Markets Association in Toronto, at 0950 EDT/1350 GMT.

Boston Federal Reserve President Cathy Minehan participates in a luncheon panel, "What are the challenges facing women in business," sponsored by Harvard University's Kennedy School of Government, at 1215 EDT/1615 GMT.
